stories.title: Iran and Oman close to Hormuz plan but await US agreement
stories.summary: Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and were finalising arrangements for jointly managing the strategic waterway, Tehran said, even as fresh security incidents highlighted continued risks for regional shipping. The agreement would be a step towards reopening the key energy route, but official sources briefing Iranian media stressed that any easing still hinged on Washington ending its own naval blockade of Iran's ports. Iran has exercised de facto control of the waterway and threatened any vessels transiting routes it deems unauthorised ever since the US and Israel launched their war against the country on 28 February. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly insisted Tehran is keen for a deal to reopen Hormuz, but Iran has denied this and said it will instead make arrangements with its neighbour across the strait, Oman.

stories.title: July was among hottest, driest and sunniest on record
stories.summary: New statistics show that last month was one of the hottest, driest and sunniest months on record for Ireland. According to Met Éireann's climate statement for last month, July 2026 was the second hottest July on record since 1900. The forecaster has said the month was dominated by high pressure, which resulted in a national mean July temperature of 17.25C. This has only ever been topped by the mean temperature for July 2013 of 17.34C.

stories.title: Tensions cool between EU and Spain over crisis in Ceuta
stories.summary: The Government will likely breathe a sigh of relief as the political temperature surrounding Spain's handling of the migrant crisis in Ceuta cools after some fractious exchanges among EU member states in recent days. Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan was forced to convene an emergency meeting of EU interior and justice ministers after the images of over 50,000 people swimming across the border from Morocco to the Spanish North African territory pushed immigration to the top of the agenda for Ireland's EU Presidency. This morning's meeting came with Spain on the offensive - expressing annoyance at the lack of solidarity from other EU members and accusing some of turning the crisis into an attack on its Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Others wanted swift action against Madrid - with Italy and Denmark last week advocating for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-travel area over the crisis; 20 other countries joined them in saying the EU should continue pressing their tough line on immigration, seemingly at odds with Spain's open stance on migration.

stories.title: Services sector growth hits 8-month high in July - PMI
stories.summary: The country's services sector posted its fastest growth in eight months in July on stronger new business and employment, and easing inflationary pressure, a survey showed today. The AIB S&P Global Services Purchasing Managers' Index climbed to 55.2 in July from 54.2 in June, remaining well above the 50 level that separates growth from contraction. The rate of growth in the Irish services sector was well ahead of the flash euro zone, British and US PMIs. Today's survey showed that new export business expanded at the fastest pace since December 2024.

stories.title: Hormuz deal would give Iran control of inbound traffic
stories.summary: A proposed deal between Iran and Oman to help end five months of war between Iran and the United States would give Tehran control over ships entering the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, a senior Iranian source and two regional officials said, one of the biggest concessions yet to Iran. There was no immediate US comment on the proposal, and while US President Donald Trump has said a deal reopening the strait is imminent, US officials have repeatedly insisted they would never agree to Iran controlling access to the world's most important trade route for energy supplies. An agreement that gives Iran any control over access to the strait would mean the war launched by the United States and Israel in February had resulted in a major shift in the balance of regional power in Tehran's favour. Before the war, the strait was freely open to all ships with no fees.

stories.title: Salah in Istanbul to finalise Trabzonspor switch
stories.summary: Mohamed Salah has arrived in Istanbul wearing a Trabzonspor shirt to finalise a move to the Turkish Super Lig side. Hundreds of fans were on hand to greet the former Liverpool forward at Ataturk Airport after the club announced on Tuesday evening that he would travel to Trabzon via Istanbul. In a video posted on the club's social media accounts, Salah said: "Trabzon, are you ready? I can hear you. See you very soon." The 34-year-old is a free agent after leaving Liverpool this summer following nine years at the club, where he scored 257 times in 442 appearances and won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

stories.summary: NI Music Prize-nominated indie-pop artist Reevah (AKA Aoife Boyle) has just released her introspective new single, The Hardest Part. I really loved Hamnet, directed by Chloé Zhao. I went to see this in the cinema when it came out. Jessie Buckley's performance was brilliant: raw, emotional, and completely captivating. It's one of those films that stays with you long after you’ve watched it, and those are always the stories I connect with most. I found myself thinking about it for days afterwards. I’m a huge fan of CMAT and her EURO-COUNTRY album. Much like the music I write, and my latest single, I love that blend of country and indie-pop, especially when it's rooted in great storytelling. I'm always drawn to songs that have something to say. Like the rest of the world, I'm also completely here for Olivia Dean! Alongside that, I'm constantly listening to great Irish artists like Joshua Burnside, Alana Henderson, Fontaines D.C., CHALK, Sorcha Richardson and Soda Blonde, to name just a few.

stories.summary: Sombr has said he has "issues with eating" and that it has been a "lifelong" issue for the singer. The 21-year-old singer, whose real name is Shane Boose, shot to fame following the release of his 2024 song Back to Friends and is known for his pop-rock look and tracks including Undressed, 12 to 12 and Homewrecker. The sharp pivot into the spotlight, however, has been challenging for the singer, who says he has had to learn how to navigate the "weird" side of the internet where "creepy people say creepy things". One of which is his body image – something Boose said he has struggled with and sings about in his recent single My Body Isn't Ready.

stories.title: What does power dressing look like in 2026?
stories.summary: The words 'power dressing' immediately bring to mind sharp suits and big shoulders, but where does the concept originate from, and what does it look like for us today? Fashion historian Laura Fitzachary joined Doireann Garrihy to discuss the history of power dressing amongst the political class. Listen back above. Far from the sell-sell-sell power brokers of the 1980s, Fitzachary says that "if you're looking at it from a historical point of view, you could argue that it comes from the emergence of royal portraiture, court portraiture. That's where you really see people depicted in their finery, in a lot of detail." In this era, power was best signposted by the medium of painting, where one artist could be brought in to paint a subject's face and hands, while any amount of specialist painters would be brought in to depict the intricate clothing they wore, from lace and velvet to shining pearls.

stories.title: No HAP properties to rent outside Dublin, Kildare in June
stories.summary: No properties were available to rent within Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) limits outside of Dublin or Kildare in June, according to a new report from the Simon Communities of Ireland. Its latest 'Locked Out of the Market' report found that just 20 properties were available to rent under HAP scheme limits in 16 areas they surveyed during that month. HAP is a form of social housing support provided by local authorities in Ireland, which allows tenants to receive financial support towards their rent while still being able to work. The scheme allows local authorities to make monthly rental payments directly to a landlord on behalf of a tenant. In return, the HAP tenant pays a weekly rent contribution to the local authority.

stories.title: Christian Brothers' focus on claims 'without litigation'
stories.summary: The head of the Christian Brothers has said that contrary to recent commentary, the focus of the congregation remains "resolutely on settling claims in a timely manner without the stress and delays of litigation". In a statement, Br David Gibson said that in addition to contributions to Redress and Statutory Funds, the congregation had provided compensation of over €40 million including legal fees to over 200 claimants, and provided counselling for the survivors of abuse. Br Gibson said that the typical approach of the congregation was to acknowledge a claim with an offer of mediation, and he confirmed that at present, a majority of notified claims are settled within 12 months "without the stress of a court appearance". In the statement, he said claimants were listened to in a non-adversarial setting, and their claims were settled in a timely manner.

stories.title: Donald Trump set to travel to Doonbeg for Irish Open
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Ireland next month for a visit that will include his attendance at the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg, Co Clare, and events in Dublin. This date is to ensure he will be in the US for the annual commemoration of the 11 September terrorist attacks, and that he will be in Doonbeg in time for the end of the Irish Open on 13 September. Mr Trump's visit will also include a trip to Dublin, which is likely to involve a meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin. However, sources said it is highly unlikely that Mr Trump will give a speech to the Dáil or Seanad, or attend any events at Leinster House, as TDs and senators are not due to return from their summer break until 16 September.

stories.title: Glanbia half-year revenue rises 7%, lifts outlook
stories.summary: Shares in nutrition supplement maker Glanbia jumped nearly 8% in Dublin trade this morning after it reported higher revenues and profits for the six months to the end of June and said it was upgrading its full year guidance. Glanbia's half year revenues rose by 7% to $2.1 billion from $1.9 billion the same time last year, while group pre-exceptional profit after tax jumped by 34.4% to $175.4m from $132m on a constant currency basis. EBITDA for the six month period rose by 14.1% to $275.4m from $241.3m the same time last year. Glanbia also reported adjusted earnings per share of 81.24 US cents, an increase of 30% on the 63.03 US cents reported in 2025.

stories.title: Israel resumes Lebanon strikes as talks under way in Rome
stories.summary: Israel's military resumed strikes on southern Lebanon despite ongoing talks, blaming a ceasefire violation by militant group Hezbollah as Beirut said at least one person was killed. The fresh strikes and a first evacuation warning in weeks came as Lebanon and Israel were holding US-sponsored talks in Rome aimed at putting an end to hostilities, with Beirut seeking Israel's phased withdrawal from the south. "In response to a blatant violation of the ceasefire by the Hezbollah terrorist organisation, the IDF has begun conducting precise strikes in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement, shortly after telling residents to evacuate the town of Mansouri in the south. Lebanese state media said one person died and 11 were wounded in a separate strike.

stories.title: Healy's head and heart call on Birmingham double bid

Healy has competed predominately in the 1500m in recent years, but claimed an impressive European U18 double back in 2018, winning both the metric mile and 3000m in Gyor. Seven years later, Healy was back on the top of the podium, again over 3000m, at the European indoor championships in Apeldoorn, becoming the first Irish woman to do so. Few manage to convert underage success into senior glory, but Healy achieved it. It was however a journey that wasn’t without its challenges, and the 25-year-old felt none of her competitors resented her historic win in the Netherlands.

stories.summary: The sun shone brightly overhead on what would be the last day in the blue of Dublin for Ciarán Kilkenny. Perhaps it was fitting the old rivals Kerry provided the opposition. After all it was a glorious career, with eight All-Ireland medals in his pocket. Throughout his career, Kilkenny has made no secret of his love for American sports and the Castleknock native is ambassador for the upcoming Aer Lingus College Football Classic at the Aviva Stadium on 29 August. At a media event ahead of the game between Texas Christian University's Horned Frogs and University of North Carolina’s Tar Heels, the now former Dubs star always had it in his mind that 2026 would be his last season wearing the blue.

stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers manager Stephen Bradley admitted to feeling frustrated despite his side's 3-1 victory over Albanian outfit Egnatia in the Europa League third qualifying round. Pico Lopes fired the Hoops back in front from Jack Byrne’s pass in the 56th minute before Aaron Greene netted two minutes later to put them in control ahead of the return leg in Albania. However, Rovers could and should have added to their lead as Burke, Jonathan Afolabi and Jake Mulraney all had big chances to cap off an impressive second-half display with further goals.

stories.title: Ospreys or Scarlets face axe as WRU outlines cut plans
stories.summary: Wales are to go ahead with plans to cut their number of professional franchises from four to three, spelling the end for either the Ospreys or Scarlets, both former winners of the United Rugby Championship. The Welsh Rugby Union on Wednesday confirmed the proposed change to the professional game and plans to establish three men's teams from the 2028/29 season – one based in the capital, one in west Wales and one in east Wales. Cardiff, owned by the Welsh Rugby Union, and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences, leaving Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the remaining spot. Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.title: 10 must-see shows at Dublin Fringe Festival 2026
stories.summary: In her 2nd year as Dublin Fringe Festival Director, Bee Sparks highlights 10 must-see shows to consider for your festival diary this September. This is Dublin Fringe's boldest programme yet, a festival that takes over the city for 16 days and nights of exceptional, multidisciplinary work. This year the festival sets out to reignite our love affair with Dublin City, championing the irrepressible, indomitable creative force of Ireland’s artists and audiences, creating a festival that reflects the Ireland of today: the breadth of communities who call it home, the crucial conversations that shape our reality, and the visions that show us how things could be. Expect breath-taking performances across a sweeping spectrum of artforms - experience sharp new plays grappling with contemporary life - gas comedy to bring the belly-laughs - and interdisciplinary spectacle that forges new forms. The work at the festival will uncover hidden histories, bold futures and the beauty found right on your doorstep. Celebrate Ireland’s drag culture, bop to the best new hip-hop and R&B, and dance into the morning light. The best of international makes its home in Dublin this year too - from raucous gig theatre, quirky cabaret and breath-catching Zambian circus, to stepping behind the stage curtain to share your legacy with a tree. Now dive in! 1/ PHILOSOPHY OF THE WORLD from UK based live performance company, In Bed With My Brother. This is bold international work at it best and is presented in partnership with Project Arts Centre. In Bed With My Brother, have collaborations spanning theatre, performance, art, cabaret, music and nightlife, blending chaos, tongue-in-cheek humour and high-octane theatrical spectacle. Philosophy Of The World is a three-act biopic that attempts to wrangle the story of the best worst band of all time into an exciting new show for Dublin Fringe 2026. Part tribute act, part feminist reclamation, part rambling flight of ideas, this is about fate, freewill, power, patriarchy, band t-shirts, daddy issues and the best worst album ever made.

Thorne, 28, rose to fame playing CeCe Jones on the Disney Channel series Shake It Up alongside the Dune actress. The pair played best friends on the dance programme from 2010 to 2013. Despite this, Thorne claimed the teenagers were often compared to one another in the media, and by fans, because they were two young girls in the spotlight. Speaking on Alex Cooper's Call Her Daddy podcast, Thorne said "it got pretty bad" and forced the pair, aged 14, to sit down and talk it out.

stories.title: How a 200-year-old building became a coffee shop made of scrap
stories.summary: Nestled in the bustling heart of Monaghan town, Genesis is a coffee shop with a difference. Not only is it built with community in mind, driving business into a previously derelict building, but it has been handmade using repurposed objects. The sturdy floor is made from old scaffold planks and repurposed tiles; the counter is made from "a bit of a shed"; tables were carved from items found in a skip; and light fittings in the ceiling are crafted from old sewing machines. "There were a few sewing machines in the building," explains Kevin, "so I kept a bit of that history there, and converted them into lights. I made two of them and got an electrician to connect them up." Having worked on building sites for many years, Kevin McGuire says he became pretty "handy" over the years, jokingly describing himself as a 'Jack of all trades, but master of none'.

stories.summary: The funeral of Oscar-winning Irish actress Brenda Fricker will take place in Dublin this morning. The service for the 81-year-old will be held at St Catherine's Church on Meath Street at 11am, followed by a private burial. Fricker died on 16 July at Our Lady's Hospice in Harold's Cross. Born in Dublin in 1945, she had a career that spanned more than six decades across stage and screen, becoming one of Ireland's most celebrated actors.

stories.title: Unprecedented increase in UHL attendances - HSE
stories.summary: The HSE Mid-West has said issues around overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick are due to "a long-standing structural mismatch between patient demand and available capacity". The Regional Executive Management Team was responding to remarks by the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation (INMO), which said the situation "is extremely challenging and it's a constant challenge there on a daily 24-hour basis". The INMO had called for an independent examination on the presentations and decisions to admit at UHL, which HSE Mid-West says was already completed by both the Economic and Social Research Institute, and the health watchdog, HIQA. Yesterday, the INMO said there were 617 patients without a bed in hospitals around the country, with 388 patients waiting on trolleys in emergency departments and 229 patients waiting on trolleys in other hospital wards.

stories.title: Ceuta crisis puts Ireland's EU presidency to the test
stories.summary: Of all the potential flashpoints that risked overshadowing the first weeks of Ireland's EU presidency, it is safe to say Ceuta was until recently not one. The tiny Spanish territory on the north African coastline has long been a source of dispute in the region. But with Aughinish Alumina, ongoing calls for a possible EU-wide version of the occupied territories bill, social media age restrictions and domestic political matters, only the best of predictors would have suggested the autonomous location just 18.5km in size was going to garner much attention. All of that changed this week when a sudden influx of Moroccan migrants into Ceuta pushed the area directly into an EU spotlight which is unlikely to dim any time soon.

stories.title: Wizz Air sees Q1 operating loss on fuel costs, weak fares
stories.summary: Wizz Air said today that a key measure of airline sales at the budget carrier would fall in its second quarter, as soaring fuel costs and weak fares driven by the Iran war weighed on one of Europe's more vulnerable airlines. The carrier also swung to a first-quarter operating loss of €183.3m, highlighting the pressure facing European budget airlines as they are forced to absorb ballooning fuel costs while customers still demand cheap seats. Wizz Air said second-quarter revenue per available seat kilometre would fall by a low single-digit percentage year-on-year, even as it guided for seat capacity growth of up to high-twenties percentage. The company's results echo the strain flagged by rival Ryanair, and lay bare a widening split in European aviation where full-service flag carriers are proving far more resilient to the war than budget operators.

stories.title: Cahalane believes new blood can give Cork the edge
stories.summary: Méabh Cahalane is hoping that a new-look Cork side can produce a familiar result when they take on Galway at Croke Park in Sunday's All-Ireland Senior Camogie final. The Rebels are looking to claim their third O’Duffy Cup in four years, having been finalists in each of the last five championships. They’re also out for a measure of revenge against the side that narrowly beat them in last season’s final after Galway ended their three-in-a-row hopes with a one point win. Cork entered the 2025 final on the back of an unbeaten campaign and, in a nip-and-tuck game, looked to have turned things in their favour when a late goal from Orlaith Cahalane levelled the game up, only to see Carrie Dolan snatch the game with a huge injury-time point.

stories.title: Former GAA President Liam O'Neill dies
stories.summary: The Laois man, who was born in August 1955, served as the 37th President of the association and became Uachtarán-Tofa in 2011 at Congress in Mullingar. He was the first GAA President elected unopposed. He became the first person from the Leinster county to hold the honour since Robert O’Keeffe (1935-38), the Kilkenny-born hurler who is honoured with the Bob O'Keeffe Cup in the Leinster SHC. O’Neill was a former chairperson of Leinster GAA and principal of Gaelscoil Throimera, retiring from education in 2018. A former Laois county secretary, he also worked closely with the county's Cumann na mBunscol while he was also secretary and chairperson of the UCD hurling club during his student days. O'Neill also held a number of committee roles with his club Trumera. In 2018, O'Neill revealed that he was considering running for the Irish Presidency before deciding against it.
